title: Sensitivity analysis
outcome: Explain sensitivity analysis using the records and boundaries of this fictional investigation.
scenario: A decision sensitive to the cutoff. A toy score rule predicts positive when score is at least the chosen cutoff.
given: Scores are 0.4,0.6,0.8. Cutoff 0.5 marks the last two positive; cutoff 0.7 marks only 0.8 positive.

steps.label: Hold scores fixed
steps.detail: Keep the same three supplied scores.

explanation: Sensitivity analysis checks how conclusions change under plausible choices. Changing a cutoff changes the decision rule, not the recorded scores or their accuracy.

counterfactual.prediction: 0.6 and 0.8 are positive because the rule includes equality.
counterfactual.reason: The declared at-least boundary includes the threshold value.

student_task: Classify 0.4, 0.6 and 0.8 at cutoffs 0.5, 0.7 and exactly 0.6. Which equality rule decides the boundary, and can these unlabelled scores identify the best cutoff?
teacher_answer: Keep the same three supplied scores. 0.6 and 0.8 meet the boundary. Only 0.8 meets the new boundary. Changed case: 0.6 and 0.8 are positive because the rule includes equality. The declared at-least boundary includes the threshold value. At cutoff 0.6, equality passes; absent reference labels, no best cutoff is established.
project_evidence: For the Reproducible AI Research Study, retain an annotated worked trace and the changed-case reasoning. Connect the claim to its records, units and assumptions so another investigator can challenge or reproduce it.
limits: Without reference labels, these counts do not identify the best cutoff or establish correctness.
review_note: Individually authored fictional practice distinct from the reserved independent case. No invented significance, real experiment execution or pupil outcome is asserted.
